subject: math
title: Grade 5 Decimals to Thousandths
seo_title: Grade 5 Decimals to Thousandths Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on decimals to thousandths for the BC curriculum: place value charts, reading and writing decimals like 2.007, comparing and ordering, decimals and fractions such as 0.3 = 3/10, and rounding. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Tenths, hundredths and thousandths are the first, second and third places after the decimal point. 0.3 = 3/10, 0.03 = 3/100 and 0.003 = 3/1000.
key_sub: Compare by place value, not by length: 0.45 < 0.50, so 0.45 < 0.5. To round, look one place to the right: 6.381 rounds to 6.38 and 2.47 rounds to 2.5.
body_html:
Tenths, hundredths and thousandths

Split 1 whole into 10 equal parts: each part is one tenth (0.1). Split it into 100 parts: each part is one hundredth (0.01). Split it into 1000 parts: each part is one thousandth (0.001). Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

Between two hundredths there are 10 thousandths. From 0.24 to 0.25, each small space is 0.001.

Reading and writing decimals

Say “and” for the decimal point. Then read the digits after the point and say the place of the last digit. Use a 0 to hold an empty place.

DecimalIn wordsFraction
0.6six tenths610
0.45forty-five hundredths45100
2.007two and seven thousandths2 71000
0.312three hundred twelve thousandths3121000
Example 1

Write twelve and forty-six thousandths as a decimal.

Thousandths need three places after the point: 46 thousandths = 0.046.

Answer: 12.046

Comparing and ordering

Compare the whole numbers first, then the tenths, then the hundredths, then the thousandths. It helps to give the numbers the same number of places: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500.

Example 2

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from smallest to greatest.

Write them with thousandths: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Decimals and fractions

The number of places after the point tells you the denominator: one place is tenths, two places is hundredths, three places is thousandths. 0.3 = 310, 0.03 = 3100 and 0.003 = 31000. Some fractions are worth knowing by heart: 12 = 0.5, 14 = 0.25, 34 = 0.75 and 15 = 0.2.

Example 3

Write 0.125 as a fraction.

There are three places after the point, so it is thousandths.

Answer: 1251000

Rounding decimals

Find the two numbers it is between. Look at the digit one place to the right of the place you are rounding to: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. Round only once.

Example 4

Round 6.381 to the nearest hundredth.

6.381 is between 6.38 and 6.39. The thousandths digit is 1, so round down.

Answer: 6.38

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Use the same places: 0.45 < 0.50
0.3 = 3100One place after the point is tenths: 0.3 = 310
Writing twenty-three thousandths as 0.23Thousandths need three places: 0.023
Rounding 5.348 to 5.4 by rounding the 8 firstLook only at the hundredths digit: 5.348 → 5.3
Rounding 3.952 to 3.1010 tenths make 1 whole: 3.952 → 4.0

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about decimals in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 5 math curriculum includes decimals to thousandths. Students read, write, compare and order decimals like 2.635, connect them to fractions such as 0.125 = 125/1000, and round decimals.

faq.q: How do you explain thousandths to a child?
faq.a: Split a hundredth into 10 equal parts and each part is a thousandth, 0.001. On a number line from 0.24 to 0.25, the 10 small spaces are thousandths, so 7 spaces past 0.24 is 0.247.
The 5 in 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths. 0.45 is only 45 hundredths, so 0.5 is bigger even though it has fewer digits.
0.3 = 3/10, because the 3 is in the first place after the decimal point, the tenths place. 3/100 is written 0.03.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth. 7 full columns are shaded: 7 tenths = 710 = 0.7. 0.07 would be only 7 small squares, and 0.3 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: 4 full columns (4 tenths) and 3 more squares (3 hundredths) are shaded: 43 hundredths = 43100 = 0.43.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: 5 small squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 5 hundredths = 5100 = 0.05. Write a 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: 1 whole is split into 1000 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 11000 of the whole, one thousandth: 0.001. 0.01 is one hundredth (100 parts) and 0.1 is one tenth (10 parts).

items.q: How many thousandths make 1 hundredth?
items.e: Split one hundredth into 10 equal parts and each part is 1 thousandth. So 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth (0.010 = 0.01).

items.q: How many thousandths make 1 tenth?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, and each hundredth = 10 thousandths. 10 × 10 = 100 thousandths (0.100 = 0.1). 1000 thousandths make 1 whole.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2.635?
items.e: The red 5 is in the third place after the decimal point, in the thousandths column. Its value is 5 thousandths = 0.005.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 0.482?
items.e: The red 8 is in the second place after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 8 hundredths = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 3.024?
items.e: In 3.024 the 4 is in the thousandths place, the third place after the point. It is worth 0.004.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 0.951?
items.e: In 0.951 the 9 is in the tenths place, the first place after the point. It is worth 0.9.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 25.168?
items.e: In 25.168 the 2 is in the tens place (two places before the point). It is worth 20.

items.q: In 6.583, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: Count places after the decimal point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. In 6.583 the tenths digit is 5, the hundredths digit is 8 and the thousandths digit is 3. The answer is 3.

items.q: In 41.207, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: Count places after the decimal point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. In 41.207 the tenths digit is 2, the hundredths digit is 0 and the thousandths digit is 7. The answer is 0.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 14.307?
items.e: The red 3 is in the first place after the decimal point, in the tenths column. Its value is 3 tenths = 0.3. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 7.096?
items.e: The red 6 is in the third place after the decimal point, in the thousandths column. Its value is 6 thousandths = 0.006. The 0 holds the tenths place.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.24 to 0.25 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth (0.001). The dot is 7 spaces after 0.240: 0.247.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 1.3 to 1.4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth (0.01). The dot is 8 spaces after 1.30: 1.38. 1.308 would be very close to 1.3.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.06?
items.e: 1 hundredth = 10 thousandths, so 6 hundredths = 60 thousandths. 0.06 = 0.060.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.4?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 4 tenths = 400 thousandths. 0.4 = 0.400.

items.q:
Count on in thousandths. What comes next?
0.997, 0.998, 0.999, ?
items.e: 0.999 + 0.001: 9 thousandths and 1 more make 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. That makes 10 hundredths = 1 tenth, and 10 tenths = 1 whole. So the next number is 1.000 (the same as 1). There is no such step as 0.1000.

items.q: How do you read 0.6?
items.e: There is one digit after the point, so it means tenths: six tenths.

items.q: How do you read 0.45?
items.e: The last digit is in the hundredths place, so read the digits after the point as hundredths: forty-five hundredths.

items.q: How do you read 4.05?
items.e: 4 is the whole number. Say “and” for the decimal point. The 5 is in the hundredths place, so read it as four and five hundredths.

items.q: How do you read 2.007?
items.e: 2 is the whole number and “and” is the decimal point. The 7 is in the third place after the point: two and seven thousandths.

items.q: How do you read 0.312?
items.e: There are three digits after the point, so the last digit is in the thousandths place. Read the digits as a whole number, then say the place: three hundred twelve thousandths.

items.q: Write eight hundredths as a decimal.
items.e: Hundredths need two places after the point. There are 0 tenths: 0.08. 0.8 would be 8 tenths.

items.q: Write twenty-three thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: Thousandths need three places after the point. 23 fills only two, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.023. 0.23 is twenty-three hundredths.

items.q: Write five and nine tenths as a decimal.
items.e: “Five” is the whole number, “and” is the decimal point, and nine tenths is one place after the point: 5.9.

items.q: Write seven and three hundred eight thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: 7 is the whole number. Three hundred eight thousandths = 0.308 (three places after the point). So the number is 7.308.

items.q: Write twelve and forty-six thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: Forty-six thousandths needs three places: 0.046. So the number is 12.046. 12.46 is twelve and forty-six hundredths.

items.q: Write 3 ones, 4 tenths, 0 hundredths and 9 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: Write one digit in each place: 3 . 4 0 9 = 3.409. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: Write 2 tens, 6 hundredths and 5 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: 2 tens = 20. There are 0 ones and 0 tenths. Then 6 hundredths and 5 thousandths: 20.065.
4 ones, 3 tenths, 0 hundredths and 8 thousandths: 4 . 3 0 8 = 4.308.
1 ten, 0 ones, 6 tenths, 1 hundredth and 9 thousandths: 10.619.

items.q: Which shows 5.274 in expanded form?
items.e: 5 ones, 2 tenths, 7 hundredths and 4 thousandths: 5 + 0.2 + 0.07 + 0.004.

items.q: Write 0.059 in words.
items.e: There are three places after the point, so it is thousandths. The digits make 59: fifty-nine thousandths.

items.q: Which decimal has a 7 in the thousandths place?
items.e: The thousandths place is the third place after the point. In 0.427 it holds a 7. In 0.742 the 7 is in the tenths, in 0.472 it is in the hundredths, and in 7.024 it is in the ones.

items.q: Simran writes “seven and twelve thousandths” as 7.12. What should she write?
items.e: 7.12 is seven and twelve hundredths. Thousandths need three places after the point, so write a 0 first: 7.012.

items.q: A decimal has 3 ones, 15 hundredths and 2 thousandths. What is the decimal?
items.e: 15 hundredths = 0.15 and 2 thousandths = 0.002. 3 + 0.15 + 0.002 = 3.152.

items.q: Which number is 0.01 more than 4.293?
items.e: 0.01 is 1 hundredth. The hundredths digit is 9, and 9 + 1 = 10 hundredths = 1 more tenth. So 4.293 + 0.01 = 4.303. 4.294 adds 0.001 and 4.393 adds 0.1.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.5 as 0.50 so both have hundredths. 45 hundredths < 50 hundredths, so 0.45 < 0.5. Do not compare 45 with 5: the 5 in 0.5 is 5 tenths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value: 7 tenths = 70 hundredths = 700 thousandths. So 0.7 = 0.700.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 2 ones and 3 tenths. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 5. So 2.305 < 2.35, even though 2.305 has more digits.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.089 has 0 tenths and 0.1 has 1 tenth. So 0.089 < 0.1, even though 89 > 1.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 6.42 as 6.420. Both have 6 ones and 4 tenths. Compare the hundredths: 2 > 0. So 6.42 > 6.402.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the whole numbers first: 13 > 9. So 13.1 > 9.999, even though 9.999 has more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tenths: 6, 5, 5 and 0. 0.6 has the most tenths, so it is the greatest, even though 0.594 and 0.599 have more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: 0.53 has 5 tenths, so it is the greatest. The others have 3 tenths: compare the hundredths 0, 5 and 5. 0.305 has 0 hundredths, so it is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is greater than 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 = 0.250 and 0.3 = 0.300. 300 thousandths > 250 thousandths, so 0.3 > 0.25. 0.249 is 1 thousandth less than 0.25.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 400 thousandths = 0.400. Zeros at the end do not change the value. 0.04 and 0.004 move the 4 to a smaller place.

items.q: Which number is between 1.25 and 1.26?
items.e: 1.25 = 1.250 and 1.26 = 1.260. 1.257 is 1 and 257 thousandths, between 250 and 260 thousandths.

items.q: Which letter shows 0.355?
items.e: Each space is 0.01. 0.355 is halfway between 0.35 and 0.36. That is point B. A is 0.32, C is 0.37 and D is 0.395.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 0.8 = 0.80, and 80 hundredths > 79 hundredths. So 0.8 > 0.79 is true.

items.q: Hana says 0.125 > 0.2 because 125 > 2. Which is correct?
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 0.125 has 1 tenth and 0.2 has 2 tenths. So 0.125 < 0.2. Or write 0.2 as 0.200: 125 < 200 thousandths.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with thousandths: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. 405 < 450 < 500, so the order is 0.405, 0.45, 0.5. The longest number is not the greatest.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 3.2, 3.02, 3.202, 3.022
items.e: All have 3 ones. Write them with thousandths: 3.200, 3.020, 3.202, 3.022. 20 < 22 < 200 < 202 thousandths, so 3.02, 3.022, 3.2, 3.202.

items.q: Order from greatest to smallest: 0.9, 0.09, 0.909, 0.099

Which digit can go in the box to make this true?
0.6□4 > 0.67
items.e: Write 0.67 as 0.670. Both numbers have 6 tenths, so compare the hundredths. The box must be 7 or more: 0.684 > 0.670. So 8 works. With 6, 0.664 < 0.670.

items.q: Use the digits 4, 0 and 7 once each to fill 0.□□□. What is the greatest decimal you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digit in the greatest place: 7 tenths, then 4 hundredths, then 0 thousandths. The greatest decimal is 0.740.

items.q: What is the smallest number with three decimal places that is greater than 2.39?
items.e: 2.39 = 2.390. The next thousandth after 2.390 is 2.391. 2.390 is equal to 2.39, not greater, and 2.389 is less.

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 310 is 3 tenths. Tenths are the first place after the point: 0.3. 0.03 is 3 hundredths.

items.q: Write 3100 as a decimal.
items.e: 3100 is 3 hundredths. Hundredths need two places, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.03.

items.q: Write 471000 as a decimal.
items.e: 471000 is 47 thousandths. Thousandths need three places, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.047.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 has one digit after the point, so it means tenths: 0.3 = 310. 3100 is 0.03, not 0.3.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.09?
items.e: 0.09 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths: 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.125?
items.e: 0.125 has three digits after the point, so it means thousandths: 1251000. 125100 would be 1.25.

items.q: 0.6 is equal to how many hundredths?
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths. Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 60100. 6100 is only 0.06.

items.q: 0.25 is equal to how many thousandths?
items.e: 0.25 = 0.250. 25 hundredths = 250 thousandths = 2501000. 251000 is only 0.025.

items.q: Write 2 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 wholes, the decimal point, then 7 tenths: 2.7. 2.07 would be 2 and 7 hundredths.

items.q: Write 5 361000 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 wholes, then 36 thousandths. Thousandths need three places: 0.036. So the number is 5.036.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 12?
items.e: Make tenths: 12 = 510 (multiply the top and bottom by 5). 5 tenths = 0.5. 1.2 just writes the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 34?
items.e: Make hundredths: 34 = 75100 (multiply the top and bottom by 25). 75 hundredths = 0.75. 0.25 is the part that is left over (14).

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 15?
items.e: Make tenths: 15 = 210 (multiply the top and bottom by 2). 2 tenths = 0.2. 0.15 just writes the 1 and the 5 after the point.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. Which is not equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 4 full columns are shaded: 4 tenths = 40 hundredths. So 0.4, 410 and 40100 all match. 0.04 is only 4 small squares.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 1501000?
items.e: 1501000 = 0.150. A 0 at the end can be dropped: 0.150 = 0.15. 0.015 is 151000.

items.q: Which pair is equal?
items.e: 0.7 is 7 tenths, so 0.7 = 710. 0.07 is 7100 and 0.007 is 71000.

items.q: Which fraction is between 0.3 and 0.4?
items.e: 35100 = 0.35, which is between 0.30 and 0.40. 34 = 0.75, 4100 = 0.04 and 3100 = 0.03.

items.q: Compare 35 and 0.65.
items.e: Change 35 to a decimal: 35 = 610 = 0.6. 0.6 = 0.60, and 60 hundredths < 65 hundredths. So 35 < 0.65.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.6, 12, 0.45
items.e: Change 12 to a decimal: 0.5. Now compare 0.60, 0.50 and 0.45: 0.45, 12, 0.6. 12 is not the smallest just because 1 and 2 are small digits.

items.q: Ji-woo says 0.3 = 3100. What is correct?
c: 0.3 is 3 tenths, so 0.3 = 310
Ji-woo is right: 0.3 = 3100
items.e: The 3 is in the first place after the point, the tenths place. So 0.3 = 310. 3100 is 0.03 (two places).

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (2.47) to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 2.47 is between 2.4 and 2.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up to 2.5. The dot is closer to 2.5 than to 2.4.

items.q: Round 6.381 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: 6.381 is between 6.38 and 6.39. Look at the thousandths digit: 1. 4 or less, so round down to 6.38. 6.4 rounds to the nearest tenth instead of the nearest hundredth.

items.q: Round 4.65 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 4.65 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 5. The nearest whole number has no decimal places, so 4.7 is not the answer.

items.q: Round 3.952 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 3.952 is between 3.9 and 4.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 4.0. The answer is written 4.0 to show tenths. 3.10 is wrong: 10 tenths make 1 whole.

items.q: Round 7.049 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 7.049 is between 7.0 and 7.1. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 7.0. Do not round the 9 first: 7.049 is closer to 7.0 than to 7.1.

items.q: Which number rounds to 5.3 when you round to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit. 5.348 has 4 hundredths, so it rounds down to 5.3 (do not round the 8 first). 5.351 and 5.36 round up to 5.4, and 5.249 rounds to 5.2.

items.q: To round 8.274 to the nearest hundredth, which digit do you look at?
items.e: To round to the nearest hundredth, look one place to the right of the hundredths: the thousandths digit. It is 4, so 8.274 rounds down to 8.27.

items.q: A bag of trail mix for a hike in Stanley Park has a mass of 0.746 kg. What is its mass to the nearest hundredth of a kilogram?
items.e: 0.746 is between 0.74 and 0.75. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 0.75. Answer: about 0.75 kg.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Ava runs 4.386 km. How far is that to the nearest tenth of a kilometre?
items.e: 4.386 is between 4.3 and 4.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 4.4. Answer: about 4.4 km. 4.39 km is rounded to the nearest hundredth.

items.q: A salmon caught on the Fraser River has a mass of 3.752 kg. What is its mass to the nearest hundredth of a kilogram?
items.e: 3.752 is between 3.75 and 3.76. Look at the thousandths digit: 2. 4 or less, so round down to 3.75. Answer: about 3.75 kg.

items.q: In one rainy week in Vancouver, 8.47 cm of rain falls. What is that to the nearest centimetre?
items.e: 8.47 is between 8 and 9. Look at the tenths digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 8. Answer: about 8 cm. 9 cm comes from rounding twice (8.47 → 8.5 → 9). Round only once, from the tenths digit.

items.q: A loonie has a mass of 6.27 g. What is its mass to the nearest tenth of a gram?
items.e: 6.27 is between 6.2 and 6.3. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up to 6.3. Answer: about 6.3 g.

items.q: A bag of cherries at a fruit stand in the Okanagan costs $4.85. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $4.85 is between $4 and $5. Look at the tenths digit: 8. That is 5 or more, so round up to $5. $4.90 rounds to the nearest 10¢, not the nearest dollar.

items.q: At a track meet in Kamloops, Liam’s long jump is 2.45 m and Mateo’s is 2.405 m. Who jumped farther?
items.e: Write both with thousandths: 2.450 m and 2.405 m. 450 > 405 thousandths, so Liam jumped farther. 2.405 has more digits, but that does not make it greater.

items.q: Three snowboarders race at Whistler. Kai finishes in 48.36 seconds, Owen in 48.4 seconds and Zara in 48.305 seconds. Who is the fastest?
items.e: The fastest racer has the least time. Write the times with thousandths: 48.360, 48.400 and 48.305. 48.305 is the least, so Zara is the fastest.

items.q: Three sockeye salmon have masses of 2.5 kg, 2.35 kg and 2.475 kg. Order the masses from lightest to heaviest.
items.e: Write them with thousandths: 2.500, 2.350 and 2.475. 350 < 475 < 500, so the order is 2.35 kg, 2.475 kg, 2.5 kg.

items.q: On a hike up Grouse Mountain, Noah drinks 0.6 L of water and Chloe drinks 0.58 L. Chloe says she drank more because 58 > 6. Who drank more?
items.e: 0.6 L = 0.60 L. 60 hundredths > 58 hundredths, so Noah drank more. Compare place by place: 6 tenths > 5 tenths.

items.q: Hana’s water bottle holds 0.75 L. What fraction of a litre is that?
items.e: 0.75 = 75100 = 34. 751000 is 0.075, and 14 is 0.25.

items.q: A cedar seedling in a school garden in Nanaimo is 0.375 m tall. Which fraction of a metre is that?
items.e: 0.375 has three places after the point, so it means thousandths: 3751000 m. 375100 m would be 3.75 m, taller than a door.

items.q: A tent pole for a camping trip on Vancouver Island is 2.396 m long. What is its length to the nearest hundredth of a metre?
items.e: 2.396 is between 2.39 and 2.40. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 2.40. Answer: 2.40 m. 9 hundredths and 1 more make 10 hundredths, which is 1 more tenth. 2.310 is wrong: 10 hundredths cannot go in one place.
